dimensions.name: Contract & semantics reconnaissance

evidence.note: Stated up front that the key is to match helpers.py exactly before choosing implementation shape — reconnaissance-first framing.
Read helpers.py in full (all endpoints, patch/csv/xlsx client methods, {workbooks:[]} envelope), plus run.sh and conftest, pinning the wire contract.

Systematically read every public test file — engine, spill, deps, copy_fill, sort_filter, csv, xlsx, ooxml, xlsx_oracle, collab, iter, pivot, locale, validation — extracting cell kind/display/format/style shapes, error names, and locale params.
Probed available libraries (openpyxl, formulas, xlcalculator, pycel, scipy) then synthesized the broad surface and made a deliberate evaluator/design choice.

Later 'dev_tests' interactions are all run.sh verification runs, not fresh re-reading of the client; no independent openpyxl/LibreOffice round-trip experiments or fixture inspection — short of level-10 continuous reconnaissance.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent systematically extracted the full contract from the first-party client and the entire public test corpus up front — endpoints, cell discriminators, spill/format/style fields, error names, locale params — and cross-referenced it against the spec while probing library availability, squarely matching the level-8 anchor. It stops short of level 10 because it ran no targeted openpyxl/LibreOffice round-trip or Excel-semantics experiments, never inspected the oracle fixtures, and did not return to re-read the client when reaching new subsystems (later test touches are verification runs, not reconnaissance).

dimensions.name: Subsystem decomposition & sequencing

evidence.note: Enumerates the full subsystem slice (formulas, dynamic arrays, deps, CSV/XLSX, collab, formats, pivots, locale, validation, iterative calc) and deliberately front-loads the runnable server + dependency bootstrap + foreground health endpoint before advanced features — matches the level-5 'runnable server first, rough ordering' anchor.

Explicitly sequences verification in slices ('run the visible suite in slices to fix contract/evaluator defects'): base API+engine first, then deps/spill/fill/sort/filter/csv, then xlsx/ooxml/pivot. These test slices act as independently-checkable acceptance gates in a rough dependency order, pushing above a flat feature list.

Phase transitions are dependency-aware — 'base API and public corpus passing, moving to stateful behavior next: cycles, spill, fill, sort/filter, import/export' then a distinct 'hardening pass for hidden-suite behavior'. Ordering is intentional but staged mainly as verification phases, not as an upfront milestone hierarchy with per-item done criteria.

Core implemented as a single monolithic module in one apply_patch ('intentionally one service module'), so subsystems were not built as independently-checkable milestones staged behind prerequisites — the explicit dependency-ordered milestone structure of level 8 is absent; sequencing is real but coarse.

Runs the whole suite plus a manual restart/persistence check after hardening, treating full-suite-green + restart as a final acceptance criterion — an implicit done-check tied to the grading surface, consistent with mid-scale sequencing.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent clearly beats the flat-list level-3 anchor and meets level-5: it front-loads a runnable server with health/persistence/core cells before advanced surfaces and orders work sensibly, using staged test slices as checkpoints. It edges toward level 8 because the verification phases are dependency-aware and each slice is independently checkable, but it falls short of a true explicit milestone hierarchy — the build was one monolithic module rather than subsystems staged behind their prerequisites, and there are no concrete per-milestone done-criteria defined upfront. That places the observed behavior at a 6, between the level-5 and level-8 anchors.

dimensions.name: Verification beyond the smoke suite

evidence.note: Ran /dev_tests/run.sh repeatedly — targeted subsets during debugging and the full 131-test suite twice — using green/red as milestone gates. Regular smoke-suite use (anchor 5 baseline).

Beyond just running the suite, wrote independent ad hoc probes: POSTed SUBSTITUTE/REPT formulas via the API to isolate a parser bug, and exercised the engine in-process on LET/LAMBDA cases to check semantics as features landed — ad hoc endpoint/formula checks matching anchor 5.

Built a genuine beyond-suite check: created workbook A1=41,B1=A1+1, stopped the process, restarted, and confirmed B1 still evaluated to 42 after reload. A self-directed process-restart persistence test — one of the four items anchor 8 lists — pushing above a pure smoke-suite level.

Final verification claims cover only run.sh (131 passed), the restart check, and health — no independent openpyxl re-import of exports, no performance-budget timing on the 100k/5k-dependent cases, no independent collab seq/replay or iterative-convergence checks beyond what the visible suite already runs.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent went beyond a green smoke suite: it ran run.sh regularly as a gate, wrote independent API/engine probes to isolate bugs and check formula semantics (anchor 5), and constructed a real self-directed restart/persistence test (one of the four anchor-8 items). But it built only that single beyond-suite check — no openpyxl re-import round-trip, no rough performance-budget timing, and no independent Excel-value or collab/iterative-calc verification beyond what the provided suite already exercised. That places it above the ad-hoc level of 5 but well short of the broad, self-gating targeted verification described at 8, i.e., a 6.

dimensions.name: Coverage tracking across the surface

evidence.note: One-time enumeration of the subsystem surface (REST, formulas, dynamic arrays, deps, CSV/XLSX, validation, locale, pivot, iteration, WebSockets) — a mental map of what must be covered, but never turned into a maintained remaining-work tracker.

Reads the full suite's failure set precisely (5 failed), catalogs the three distinct remaining defects, and patches each once without re-debugging loops — accurate done-vs-remaining picture within the visible suite.
Re-runs the complete public suite after fixes to confirm 131 pass, verifying earlier subsystems still hold as new fixes land — genuine regression/coverage reconciliation via the test suite as ledger.

Declares completion at 'public suite green' plus a restart/persistence check; never constructs a remaining-work map for the explicitly-warned larger hidden suite or the full 100+ function catalog, so tracking stays bounded to the visible tests.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent maintains an accurate, precise picture of progress against the public test suite — enumerating subsystems once (step 13), cataloging each remaining failure exactly (65-68), and re-running the whole suite to confirm no regressions (85-86), which matches the anchor-5 'keeps a checklist and updates it, catching most omissions' with a touch of anchor-8 regression awareness. But it never builds or continuously reconciles a remaining-work map of the full graded surface (100+ functions, hidden suite), treating public-green as the finish line, so it falls short of the accurate, self-driven coverage map the 8 anchor requires.

dimensions.name: Course-correction on divergence

evidence.note: Before committing to an approach, ran a cheap probe of which formula/OOXML libraries were installed (formulas, xlcalculator, pycel all False). Used that evidence to deliberately decide against shelling out to a spreadsheet process and build a custom evaluator instead — directly mitigating the risky 'library won't round-trip openpyxl-readably' bet. This is early risk-anticipation with a cheap probe.

Chose to run the visible suite in slices specifically so contract/evaluator defects surface quickly instead of waiting for a full run — a verification design intended to catch divergence early. Slices largely passed, so little correction was actually forced.

Restart/persistence probing: hit ModuleNotFoundError for 'requests', made a clean local swap to urllib and continued verifying persistence, delete (204), and next_id state across a real process restart. Minor, well-targeted local corrections rather than design revisions.

Edge-case probes (IFNA/NA returning wrong error, FIND/SEARCH lacking #VALUE handling, missing TRUE/FALSE/NA) drove targeted fixes for hidden-suite robustness, each followed by re-running the relevant slice (69,75). Evidence-driven but small-scale hardening, not architectural pivots.

Final state: 131 tests pass and restart persistence verified. The trajectory is notably smooth — the up-front design held, so the higher-anchor behavior of a forced clean pivot on a falsified core assumption was never exercised.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent demonstrated one clearly level-10-flavored move — anticipating the risky formula/OOXML-library bet and validating it with a cheap library-availability probe (26) before choosing a custom engine (27) — and consistently used failing/edge-case checks as signals for deliberate, targeted fixes before piling on more work (33, 66-73). However, because the initial design largely held, the trajectory never presented a major falsified assumption demanding a scoped architecture/library pivot; observed corrections were competent but small and local (urllib swap, missing functions, error sentinels). That places it above the level-5 'fix immediate cause / swap only when forced' anchor and into the level-8 'treat failing checks as signals to revise deliberately' territory, but short of the sustained, pivot-heavy level-10, since the full self-correcting-under-divergence behavior was not exercised. Net: 7.

dimensions.name: Effort allocation for graded coverage

evidence.note: Explicitly enumerated the full breadth of subsystems and stated intent to build pieces that 'fit the smoke tests and leave room for the hidden corpus' — breadth-aware framing before any code.

Deliberate breadth-first baseline: a single 1719-line patch implementing every subsystem at once (all 55+ catalog functions present, plus pivot/goal_seek/collab/xlsx/locale/validation/iterative), securing broad working coverage before any depth.

Post-baseline effort was funneled into the highest-value/riskiest core — formula parser, spill clearing, LET/LAMBDA, iterative cycles — rather than gold-plating low-leverage corners like distributions.
Reached 131/131 smoke tests then stopped and did persistence check; deepening was reactive to test failures, with no explicit value-density reallocation or conscious stubbing of low-return corners.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent secured a broad working baseline across all subsystems in a single up-front pass (stronger than the 'most major subsystems' of anchor 5) and then directed its fixes at the highest-leverage, riskiest area — the formula engine — while avoiding rabbit-holing any low-value corner, which is characteristic of anchor 8. However, the deepening was driven reactively by smoke-suite failures rather than by an explicit, continuously updated value-density weighing with deliberate time-boxing and stubbing, so it falls short of the disciplined 8-10 behavior. This lands at 7, between 'roughly balanced' and 'deliberate leverage triage.'

rubric.task_read: A very long-horizon build of a complete Excel-style spreadsheet product spanning many largely independent subsystems: persistent HTTP server, a REST contract that must be reverse-engineered from an existing client (/dev_tests/helpers.py), a 100+ function Excel-365 formula engine with dynamic-array spill/LET/LAMBDA/iterative calc/goal-seek, dirty topological recompute under hard performance budgets, XLSX/CSV round-trip graded against LibreOffice ground truth, a Playwright-targeted SPA, and WebSocket collaboration. Difficulty comes from enormous breadth, an under-specified wire contract, a non-exhaustive smoke suite versus a large hidden grading suite, and semantic fidelity to Excel. A skilled practitioner would invest heavily and continuously in all five meta-work faculties — this task sits near the ceiling of complexity.

dimensions.name: Contract & semantics reconnaissance
dimensions.description: Reverse-engineering the exact wire shapes from /dev_tests/helpers.py and probing Excel/openpyxl/LibreOffice semantics before and while building.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The JSON contract (ids, cell kinds, spill fields, patch/fill/sort/filter bodies, listing envelope) is defined ONLY by the existing client; guessing it wrong makes every endpoint fail the hidden suite regardless of internal correctness. Excel edge-case semantics and openpyxl/LibreOffice XLSX behaviour are graded cell-by-cell, so they must be studied, not assumed.

anchors.0: Starts coding endpoints/engine without reading helpers.py or run.sh; invents wire shapes and function semantics from memory.
anchors.3: Skims helpers.py once, picks up a couple of obvious shapes, but leaves most request/response bodies, cell discriminators, and spill fields inferred by guess.
anchors.5: Reads helpers.py and run.sh to pin down the main endpoints and cell shapes before building the core, and checks Excel semantics for the common functions.
anchors.8: Systematically extracts the full contract from the client (every endpoint, the kind discriminator, spill/spill_range, error names, locale params), cross-references it against the spec, and deliberately investigates hard corners (spill ghosts, LWW seq ordering, openpyxl definedName/numFmt/cellXfs requirements) before committing to a design.
anchors.10: Builds a durable, referenceable model of the entire contract and its ambiguities from the client plus targeted experiments (e.g. probing openpyxl/LibreOffice round-trip behaviour, Excel error-propagation and locale rules), continuously returning to re-read the client when a new subsystem is reached rather than acting on stale assumptions — reconnaissance that visibly prevents whole classes of contract-mismatch failures.

dimensions.name: Subsystem decomposition & sequencing
dimensions.description: Breaking the enormous surface into an ordered hierarchy of subsystems with dependency-aware sequencing and explicit done-criteria per milestone.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The product has a dozen loosely-coupled subsystems with real dependency order (server+persistence → cell model → recompute → formula engine → dynamic arrays → advanced surfaces). Attacking it as one undifferentiated push, or in the wrong order, guarantees thrash and a server that never reaches a runnable, gradable baseline.

anchors.0: No decomposition; jumps between unrelated features (a distribution function, then a WebSocket, then styling) with no ordering or completion criteria.
anchors.3: A flat undifferentiated list of features with no dependency ordering and no per-item definition of done.
anchors.5: A sensible component breakdown that front-loads a runnable server (health, persistence, core cells) before advanced features, with rough ordering.
anchors.8: An explicit dependency-ordered milestone structure where each milestone is independently checkable (e.g. 'health+persistence green', 'core patch/recompute passes run.sh', 'spill engine', 'xlsx round-trip'), and later subsystems are deliberately staged behind their prerequisites.
anchors.10: A living, hierarchical plan that sequences by both dependency and grading leverage, keeps a always-runnable server as an invariant between milestones, and is re-cut as understanding grows — each milestone carrying a concrete acceptance check that ties back to the client/hidden-suite surface.

dimensions.name: Verification beyond the smoke suite
dimensions.description: Deliberately designing checks — running run.sh, exercising helpers.py, restart/persistence tests, openpyxl re-import, Excel-value spot-checks — well beyond the non-exhaustive suite provided.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The spec explicitly warns the dev_tests are a non-exhaustive smoke suite and grading is a much larger hidden suite plus a LibreOffice ground-truth corpus. Passing run.sh proves almost nothing; only self-built verification against Excel semantics, round-trip fidelity, restart survival, and performance budgets catches the failures that actually cost points.

anchors.0: Never runs the server against the client or run.sh; assumes code is correct because it was written.
anchors.3: Runs run.sh occasionally and treats a green smoke suite as done; no independent checks of semantics, round-trip, persistence, or performance.
anchors.5: Runs run.sh/helpers.py regularly and does ad hoc manual checks of a few endpoints and formula results as features land.
anchors.8: Builds targeted checks the suite omits — Excel-value comparisons for formulas/errors, openpyxl re-import of exports, a process-restart persistence test, and at least rough checks against the performance budgets — and uses them to gate milestones.
anchors.10: Establishes a sustained verification harness spanning the graded dimensions (cell-by-cell value checks vs known Excel results, XLSX round-trip through openpyxl, collaboration seq/replay invariants, iterative-calc convergence, large-workbook timing), runs it continuously, and treats a discovered gap as a signal to strengthen the checks — verification that demonstrably surfaces defects a smoke run would miss.

dimensions.name: Coverage tracking across the surface
dimensions.description: Maintaining an accurate done-vs-remaining picture across a dozen subsystems and 100+ functions, and detecting stuck/circular states.
dimensions.why_it_matters: With a surface this large over a long horizon, it is easy to lose the plot — forget an entire subsystem (locale, pivots, data validation), silently regress an earlier one, or sink hours re-debugging one function while dozens remain. Accurate progress tracking is what keeps effort flowing to the highest-value remaining work.

anchors.0: No sense of what is done vs outstanding; features are forgotten or rediscovered by accident.
anchors.3: Vague recollection of progress; no explicit tracking, so whole areas silently go unaddressed.
anchors.5: Keeps a checklist of subsystems/functions and updates it as things are completed, catching most omissions.
anchors.8: Maintains an accurate, regularly-updated map of completed vs remaining work across all subsystems, notices when a subsystem is stalling or when a change regresses an earlier one, and reallocates rather than grinding.
anchors.10: Sustains a precise, continuously-reconciled picture of the whole surface over the long horizon — detecting circular re-debugging early, confirming earlier subsystems still pass as new ones land, and using the remaining-work map to drive sequencing decisions to the very end.

dimensions.name: Course-correction on divergence
dimensions.description: Revising design, library choices, or approach when evidence contradicts assumptions — wrong contract shape, failing round-trip, blown performance budget, broken recompute.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Big up-front bets here (formula-eval library, OOXML library, recompute architecture) can prove wrong only once exercised — a library that won't round-trip openpyxl-readably, a recompute that misses the 100k/5000-dependent budgets, a contract detail read wrong. Barrelling ahead on a falsified assumption wastes the horizon; timely correction salvages it.

anchors.0: Ignores contradicting evidence; keeps building on a broken approach even as failures accumulate.
anchors.3: Reacts only to hard crashes with local patches, never revisiting the underlying design or library choice that caused them.
anchors.5: When a check fails, diagnoses and fixes the immediate cause, and will swap an approach when clearly forced to.
anchors.8: Treats failing checks (wrong wire shape, failed round-trip, missed timing) as signals to revise the design or tooling choice deliberately, and does so before piling more work on the shaky foundation.
anchors.10: Anticipates which bets are risky, validates them early with cheap probes, and when reality diverges performs a clean, scoped pivot (architecture or library) while protecting already-working subsystems — repeatedly converting falsified assumptions into corrected direction rather than sunk-cost thrash.

dimensions.name: Effort allocation for graded coverage
dimensions.description: Allocating limited effort across a surface too large to perfect, so that broad graded coverage is secured before any one area is gold-plated.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The task is deliberately larger than can be finished flawlessly and is graded on a broad hidden suite, so the payoff structure rewards breadth-first partial credit (many subsystems working plausibly) over depth-first perfection of a few — a genuine allocation decision distinct from mere ordering.

anchors.0: Sinks the whole budget into one subsystem (e.g. exhaustively perfecting statistics/distributions) leaving most of the product unbuilt.
anchors.3: Follows the spec top-to-bottom with no regard for value density, over-investing in low-leverage corners while high-value subsystems go missing.
anchors.5: Roughly balances effort, getting most major subsystems to a working state before polishing.
anchors.8: Deliberately triages by graded leverage — secures a broad working baseline across all subsystems first, then deepens the highest-value or riskiest areas, consciously time-boxing rabbit holes.
anchors.10: Runs a disciplined value-density allocation throughout: continuously weighing remaining effort against expected graded coverage, deferring or stubbing low-return corners, and reallocating as new information about difficulty and payoff arrives — maximising total coverage under the horizon rather than local perfection.
